bench-harness||Ürün-default sapması #3:.verify_reason: WIRE requires 'spec-required + disconnected'. The mechanism is neither disconnected nor incomplete in the product: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:204 sets `fec_loss_risk: FecLossRiskConfig::bounded_v1()` in RuntimeConfig::default(), and runtime.rs:843 `session.sender_mut().set_fec_loss_risk(cfg.fec_loss_risk)` is a real product hop into the arbiter's speculative lane. It is product-wired and default-on, i.e. SHIP. What the finding actually establishes — and establishes correctly, with a clean negative grep — is a HARNESS-FIDELITY defect: the shipped configuration is not the one any bench arm constructs. Classifying it WIRE mislabels a measurement gap as a v1 product-wiring blocker, which would wrongly imply the FEC v1 closure decision is unimplemented. Correct framing: mechanism SHIP; separately-recorded bench defect 'bench cannot instantiate the shipped speculative policy without five manual flags'.

The accumulation code is wired and works, so this is 'spec-required but incorrectly connected', which is the WIRE bucket, not SHIP-with-a-note. Downgrading also keeps it adjacent to the partial-block WIRE record, which is the same §3/§6 defect family (both stem from close-on-K-only).
